h1: How to automate data entry between two apps
answer: Pick the source of truth and a key both apps share, such as an email, map each field, and use create-or-update so nothing is entered twice.
Run it beside manual entry for a week first.

method.h2: How to automate data entry between apps, step by step

steps.title: Find the trigger in the source app
steps.body: The event that means "new record": a form submitted, an order placed, a row added. In viaSocket's catalog Facebook Lead Ads has "New Lead Submitted".

steps.title: Use create-or-update in the destination
steps.body: HubSpot has "Create or Update Contact". Where an app has only "Create", add a find step first and stop if the record exists.

note.text: Some triggers never skip repeats, so the same person can arrive twice. Create-or-update on a key is the fix in every tool.

steps.title: Clean values on the way
steps.body: Trim spaces, lower-case emails, fix date formats, split names. Most "the automation broke" reports are a format the second app rejected.

steps.title: Test with 10 to 20 real records
steps.body: Include awkward ones: no phone, a name with three parts, an email in capitals.

steps.title: Run it beside manual entry, then stop typing
steps.body: Compare the two for a week. When they match, switch off the manual step.

steps.title: Backfill old records separately
steps.body: Import the history once, by file, and let the automation handle new records only.

captain.line: Captain reads one real lead from your form to see the fields, maps them, and tests the steps on it. Writing to your own CRM runs without asking.
captain.ask: Set up an automation: every new Facebook lead is added to HubSpot as a contact, or updated if the email already exists

wrong.title: Ping-pong between two apps
wrong.body: App A updates B, which updates A, forever. Run one direction only, or skip changes made by the automation itself.

wrong.title: A field the other app does not have
wrong.body: Data drops without a sound. List every source field in the map, and put the ones with no home in a notes field.

wrong.title: Dates in the wrong format
wrong.body: 03/04 is March in one app and April in another. Convert to an unambiguous format on the way.

wrong.title: A backfill hits rate limits
wrong.body: Pushing 5,000 old records through an automation trips the destination's limits. Import history by file instead.

faqs.q: Can I sync two apps both ways?
faqs.a: You can, but it is a different job: you need a rule for which change wins, and a guard against loops. Start one way, and add the other direction only if you truly edit in both.

faqs.q: How do I stop duplicate records?
faqs.a: Match on a key both apps share, such as email or order number, and use create-or-update. Where the destination has only create, find first and skip if it exists.

faqs.q: What if the data needs judgement, like sorting free text?
faqs.a: Add an AI step for that one field, for example "sort this message into billing, bug or question", and keep the rest of the steps fixed.

faqs.q: What if a field exists in one app but not the other?
faqs.a: Decide on the field map before you build. Either create the field in the destination app, put the value in a notes field, or leave it out on purpose. A gap you chose beats one you find later.

faqs.q: How do I move the records I already have?
faqs.a: Import the history once, by file, and let the automation handle new records only. Running a big backfill through the automation can hit the apps' rate limits.

faqs.q: Why did my automation stop adding records?
faqs.a: Usually a value the second app rejected: a date in the wrong format, a phone without a country code, an email in capitals. Clean values on the way, and test with awkward records.
